children.text: A three-tiered curtain waterfall about
high and about
wide, considered the widest waterfall in the Philippines. You can ride a bamboo raft right up to the pouring water, and on clear days between
a rainbow hangs over the spray.
Tinuy-an Falls lies in the tropical rainforest of Burboanan village, Bislig City, Surigao del Sur, on the eastern edge of Mindanao. It is said to be about
high and about

wide, and instead of falling in a single stream, the water pours across its whole width like a white curtain. Because it is counted as the widest waterfall in the country, Filipinos call it the "Little Niagara of the Philippines." The falls are usually described as having three tiers, with one more, less conspicuous tier said to exist, and since sources count the tiers differently, the stated height also ranges from
to
depending on the source.

The name "Tinuy-an" comes from the Cebuano word "Tinuyo-an," meaning something done deliberately and with purpose, and in Filipino it is also compared to "Babalik-balikan," meaning a place you keep coming back to. According to legend, the people of Mount Magdiwata, who were once forced to serve as slaves of a tribe from the Agusan side, jumped into the water while riding a bamboo raft (gakit), pushed the raft toward the falls to send their masters over, and won their freedom. The falls are managed jointly by the Bislig City tourism office and the Manobo tribal council. Bislig is called the easternmost city in the Philippines, and thick forest remains around the falls.
In

, this forest was designated one of three protected areas in the Caraga region under the Expanded NIPAS Act (Republic Act No. 11038), and the regional Environment and Natural Resources office reported confirming 91 animal species and 144 plant species (33 of them near threatened). It also became famous among birdwatchers. In
February 2024

, American birder Peter Kaestner spotted an Orange-tufted spiderhunter in a heliconia thicket beside the falls, recording the world's 10,000th bird species seen, the first person ever to do so, as officially recognized by Guinness World Records.

The way from the entrance down to the water is a maintained path with steps, so children and older visitors can manage it, and half a day is enough, though you could spend a whole day here without getting bored. Many travelers tour the Surigao del Sur east coast together with
Enchanted River
and
Britania Islands

, which makes this a good fit for waterfall photo lovers, families, and birdwatchers. It is a remote place, though, nearly half a day by bus from either Davao or Butuan, so allow plenty of time in your schedule.

blocks.title: To the foot of the falls by bamboo raft

children.text: A raftsman poles you right up to the front of the falls, where the spray comes pouring down. One ride takes about
30 min
, and the fare is
per raft (about 7 people); you must wear a life vest. You will get soaked, so put electronics in a waterproof bag.
On clear days around

, when sunlight strikes the spray, a rainbow hangs in front of the wall of the falls. The rocks at the water's edge directly facing the falls and the raft itself are good spots to capture the rainbow and the falls together, but it is hard to see on cloudy mornings after heavy rain the day before.
The widest pool below the falls has clear, cool water that is especially welcome on a hot day. Wear a life vest (about
), swim only in the calmer edge areas where the current is weak, and do not go right under the falls.

Climb the concrete steps beside the falls to see the small cascades of the upper tier and a shallow natural pool. The rocks at the edge are slippery with moss, so it is best to go up with a local guide, and the guide's fee is usually handled as a tip.

When the raft gets close to the falls, the pouring spray and water pound your shoulders and feel like a natural massage. Where the flow is strong, the raftsman only goes as close as a set distance, so follow his instructions.
There are huts and tables in front of the falls where you can eat lunch while looking at the falls. They are known to cost about
per hut, and on weekends local families take the spots first.

The path from the entrance to the falls and the forest around them are full of heliconia, ferns, tropical birds, and butterflies. Birdsong is most active just after sunrise, so arrive early in the morning and walk slowly.

The shallow riverbed in front of the falls has exposed rocks, so it is a good place to set up a tripod and use a long exposure to make the water look like silk. When the water volume is lower, you can even try for the falls' reflection in the pool.
Set out from your lodging in Mangagoy, Bislig, by habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) or tricycle. It takes about
30 min–1 hr
to reach the falls.
After passing the welcome arch, you arrive at the parking area about 5 minutes later, pay the
entrance fee, and walk down to the falls.
Take photos of the whole view and the reflection from the water's edge in front of the falls in the quiet morning hours.
During the
rainbow window, ride a raft up to the front of the falls.
Put on a life vest and swim in the pool, or rest on the rocks by the water.
Climb the side steps with a guide to look around the upper-tier falls.
Have lunch at a cottage with a packed lunch you bought beforehand, or with food from the stalls at the entrance.
Head back to Mangagoy, or continue on to
Enchanted River
Leave Mangagoy and head for the falls. The key is to arrive before the rainbow window.
Enter, and finish the raft ride, swimming, and upper-tier sightseeing within the morning.
Leave the falls and head for Hinatuan. It is about
1 hr 30 min
by car from the falls to Enchanted River.
Have lunch at a restaurant near the Enchanted River entrance.
Admire the sapphire-colored water at Enchanted River and check the fish feeding time.
Return to Bislig, or spend the night in Hinatuan.
The fish feeding time at Enchanted River has shifted between noon and 3 PM, so check that day's time on the spot and plan your order accordingly.

If heavy rain the day before has suspended rafting and swimming, switch to enjoying the falls from the viewpoint and enter early to wait for the water to clear. If the rain clears in the afternoon, return to Mangagoy, walk the coastal bay walk, and finish the day with seafood for dinner.
Bislig Airport has a concrete runway, but it is mostly used by charter and small aircraft, and the direct Cebu–Bislig flight has been suspended and resumed repeatedly. On
September 20, 2024
, Leading Edge Air Services reopened the direct Cebu route twice a week, on Fridays and Sundays, with an ATR 72-500 (departing Cebu at 6 AM, about
1 hr 17 min
, regular one-way fare about
). I could not confirm the operating status after that, so check with the airline or a Bislig City announcement before booking.
The realistic way is to fly to Davao or Butuan and continue overland. From Manila, Davao takes about
2 hr
and Butuan about
1 hr 30 min
, and from Cebu, Butuan takes about
55 min
. Davao has far more flights, while Butuan is closer to Bislig by road.
From Davao, Bachelor Express air-conditioned buses run daily to Bislig from the Ecoland Bus Terminal. An information site (updated
June 2026
) lists departures at 5 AM and 8 AM, about
9 hr
, and a fare of about
, while a
review reported about
4–5 hr
for
. It varies greatly with the number of stops and the route, so plan on 4 to 9 hours; the option of transferring at Monkayo takes about
5 hr
From Butuan, it takes about
4–5 hr
from the terminal via Trento to Mangagoy, and according to a
review, bus and airport van fares were about
. From Tandag it is also 4 to 5 hours away. Either way, leave in the morning so that you arrive before dark, and get off in Mangagoy town or at the Bislig City bus terminal.
From Mangagoy town to the falls is about
17km
and takes
30 min–1 hr
, with some sections unpaved. A round-trip habal-habal costs about
including waiting time (per a
review), and a full-day charter started from about
for a motorcycle and about

for a tricycle in the same review, though prices may have gone up since. Reviews mention that drivers in town quote a high price at first, so confirm the price, waiting time, and return time before setting off.
Some reviews say you can also reach it in about
1 hr
by jeepney or multicab from the Bislig jeepney terminal, but trips are infrequent. To combine it with Enchanted River on the same day, a full-day charter is the most efficient.

items.title: By private car or rental car

children.text: The road is mostly concrete-paved up to the falls entrance, and searching Google Maps for "Tinuy-an Falls" will guide you. The parking area is about 5 minutes further in from the welcome arch, and parking costs about
. In the rainy season the mountain road can get muddy and have rockfalls, so drive only in daylight.
From Hinatuan and Enchanted River it is about
1 hr 30 min
by car, and from Siargao it takes nearly a full day via Surigao City and Butuan, so a day trip is difficult.

The Surigao del Sur east coast, where Bislig is located, is the rainiest part of the Philippines. The Hinatuan station nearby reported an average annual rainfall of about 4,554 mm, the highest in the Philippines, and the Bislig climate table also shows about 4,198 mm a year. With a Type II climate with no distinct dry season, rain is most concentrated from
November
to
January
; according to the climate table,
January
rainfall is about 710 mm and
December
about 604 mm, while
August
is about 171 mm and
July
about 183 mm.
So the relatively drier
May
October
is the safest choice, and especially
June
September

has many clearing skies, with clear water and a higher chance of seeing the morning rainbow. The falls never dry up and have the most water in the rainy season, so some who want to see a "mighty waterfall" choose
July
December
, but the water turns muddy and rafting and swimming are often suspended for safety. Even on clear days, clouds tend to build around midday, so it is better to arrive early in the morning.
September 16
is the Bislig City founding anniversary period, and on
September 17
the Tinuy-an Sayaw Festival, named after the falls, is held, so lodging and transport get crowded. Local visitors also flock here on weekends, holidays, and during the
April
May
school break, so a weekday morning is recommended.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Relatively less rain (climate table about 170–270 mm a month), many clear days
Expect rafting, swimming, and the morning rainbow. The safest time, though the mid-September festival period is crowded
Heaviest rain from the northeast monsoon (about 320–710 mm a month)
Maximum water volume, but the water is muddy, rafting and swimming are often suspended, watch for flooded roads
A transition period as rain eases (about 340–530 mm a month)
The weather changes day to day, so pick a clear day to visit; during the April school break, go on a weekday at dawn

items.label: Accommodation
items.note: In Mangagoy town, depending on room class

children.text: Prices are rough estimates as of
and may vary with local conditions.
The most convenient place to stay is Mangagoy, Bislig's commercial center. The bus terminal, market, restaurants, banks, and ATMs are close, and there are pension houses and mid-range hotels at

per night. There is also small-scale lodging of a few huts right beside the falls, but with few rooms and irregular operation, you need to check ahead. If you are also visiting Enchanted River, staying at a coastal resort on the Hinatuan side is another option.

There are stalls at the falls entrance selling meals, drinks, and souvenirs, but many people buy grilled chicken or fish, rice, and fruit at the Mangagoy market and eat them at a cottage. Bislig is a coastal city, so seafood such as crab, shrimp, and shellfish is cheap, and kinilaw (raw fish dressed in vinegar) and grilled pork are common.
To see the morning rainbow, pass through the entrance before
9 AM
and pick a clear day with no rain the day before.
The entrance fee, raft, life vest, cottage, and guide tip are all cash and cards cannot be used, so bring plenty of small bills such as
, and
. Withdraw cash at an ATM in Mangagoy beforehand.
Rafting soaks you completely, so wear a rash guard over your swimsuit and put your phone and camera in a waterproof bag.
The rocks in front of the falls and on the upper tier are very slippery with moss, so wear water shoes or strap sandals.
A wide-angle lens captures the full width, and with a tripod and an ND filter, long-exposure shots are easy. A
review said there were no restrictions on drones, but this is a protected area, so follow the on-site instructions.
Go up to the upper tier with a guide, and tip the guide as much as you feel is deserved.
Agree on a return time with your habal-habal driver in advance and get his phone number. A review says there is signal from all carriers, but it can get weak in front of the falls.
When combining it with
Enchanted River
on the same day, the two are about
1 hr 30 min
apart by car, so schedule the falls in the morning and Enchanted River in the afternoon.
Weekend afternoons are crowded with families, so a weekday morning is recommended.

After heavy rain, the water volume at the falls rises sharply and the current becomes very strong. If the caretaker suspends swimming or rafting, always comply, and do not enter the stream falling directly below the falls. The edge of the upper tier is slippery with fast water, so do not swim there.
A life vest is required for swimming and rafting, and in deep areas and strong-current zones follow the signs and the caretaker's instructions.
The falls and forest are a protected area, so take your trash back with you and do not use soap or shampoo or collect plants or animals.
Operations have stopped suddenly before. It was closed for road works from
June 4, 2018
to
August 1
, and in
December 2022
it was temporarily closed because of access negotiations between the local government and the Manobo tribal council, then reopened on
December 21
. Check the Bislig City tourism office announcements before you leave.
Entrance fees, operating hours, and activity fees can change. The schedule differs by review, and I could only confirm that entry is possible from early morning, so check the latest announcement.
In the rainy season, landslides and flooding can occur on the mountain road, so leave extra time in your long-distance bus schedule and avoid traveling at night.
There are travel advisories for parts of Mindanao, so check the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs' overseas travel safety information before departure.
About
1 hr 30 min
by car (Hinatuan). A river leading to a sapphire-colored spring whose bottom cannot be seen.
About
3–4 hr
by car (San Agustin), then an island-hopping bangka tour. Clear seas dotted with small islands, usually set aside as a separate day.
It takes nearly a full day, going via Butuan and Surigao City and then taking a boat. An island of surfing and island hopping.
About
4–9 hr
by bus. The largest city in Mindanao, famous for Mount Apo, the Philippine Eagle Center, and durian.
A coastal promenade close to Mangagoy, good for an evening stroll at sunset after you finish the falls itinerary.
